surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $93.4 million, above the preview’s $90.5–92.5 million base-case range and $90.92 million consensus estimate. The beat was modest relative to the base-case ceiling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2027 revenue reached a record $93.4 million,” up 17.7% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $90.92M” consensus; the revenue-line base case estimated “$90.5–92.5M.”

surprises.description: Management raised FY2027 revenue guidance to $374–378 million, above the existing $368–373 million range and the preview’s base-case expectation of a high-end nudge or a range around $370–374 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year FY2027 revenue guidance to $374-378 million (from $368-373 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a reiteration of $368–373M” would disappoint and its base case anticipated the range being “nudged to the high end or trimmed to $370–374M.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin reached 25.9%, well above the preview’s roughly 22% base case and even above its bull-case threshold of 23%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA hit a record $24.1 million at 25.9% of revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “adj. EBITDA ~22%”; its bull case called for “Adj. EBITDA ≥23%.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted EBITDA target was raised to 25% of revenue rather than holding at 24%, as the preview’s base case expected. Management also gave a pronounced quarterly profile: Q3 only slightly above 22%, then Q4 approaching 30%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised adjusted EBITDA guidance “to 25% of revenue (from 24%)”; it expects Q3 “only slightly north of 22%” and Q4 “to approach 30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the 24% target was expected to be “held with an H2 bridge” in its base case, and noted that H2 would need to average “~26.4%” to meet it.

surprises.description: The company now expects subscription revenue growth to exit FY2027 at 38–39%, supported by roughly $3.5–3.7 million of sequential go-live additions each quarter. The preview anticipated back-half acceleration but did not lay out an exit rate this strong and specific.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects the subscription revenue exit growth rate to reach 38-39% in Q4,” driven by “roughly $3.5-3.7 million” of sequential go-live additions per quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the 32% full-year subscription bar was “explicitly back-half weighted” and that a Q2 print around 32% would put the ramp “on schedule.”

surprises.description: Product revenue came in just under $12 million, above the preview’s $9.5–10.5 million estimate, and product backlog ended 90% higher year-over-year—stronger product demand and forward visibility than the preview’s “lumpy hardware” framing suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product revenue was just under $12 million (highest in nearly 3 years), and product backlog ended 90% higher year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Product | $9.5–10.5M” and described it as “Lumpy hardware; not the signal.”

surprises.description: Domestic HRC sales rose 33% and set a record roughly 23% above the previous peak, a notable result not quantified in the preview’s discussion of Marriott or other demand drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Domestic HRC sales rose 33% year-over-year and set an all-time record, roughly 23% above the prior peak set two years ago.”

surprises.description: Food service management sales jumped 42%, a strong result the preview did not specifically anticipate or quantify.
Asia Pacific sales grew 47%, a stronger quantified proof point than the preview’s general discussion of APAC wins and challenges getting included in regional RFPs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “difficulty getting included in European and APAC RFPs” and described APAC wins as “the proof points,” but gave no sales-growth expectation.

surprises.description: First-half free cash flow more than doubled year-over-year, a stronger cash-generation result than the preview’s discussion of the Q1 FCF swing and prior-year Q2 cash flow established as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half free cash flow more than doubled to $22.1 million from $10 million a year earlier.”
